chunks: At'tab ibn Muhammad al-Waramini al-Hafiz narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abdul Rahman ibn Maghra narrated to us, saying: Mujalid narrated to us, from Amir, from Masruq, said Attab ibn Muhammad. And Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Hafs, saying: Hamzah ibn Awun narrated to us, from Abu Usamah, from Mujalid, saying: He informed us, Amir from Masruq.

He said: A man came to Ibn Mas'ud and asked him: 'Has your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) told you how many successors he will have after him?' He replied: 'Yes. No one had asked me about it before you, and indeed you are the youngest of the people in age.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'After me, there will be as many as the chiefs of the Israelites after Moses (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.مُسْرُوقٍ: Masruq, a companion of Ibn Mas'ud

ai.seo_question: How many successors did the Prophet Muhammad predict after him according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal highlights the Prophet’s comparison of the twelve successors to the twelve chiefs (nuqaba') of the Israelites, a parallel that underscores the continuity of divine leadership across prophetic traditions. In Shia scholarship, this hadith is often cited to validate the number twelve for the Imams, linking the spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt to the established leadership structure of Bani Israel. The mention of 'nuqaba' emphasizes their role as leaders and guides, reinforcing the theological concept of Imamate as a divinely appointed institution.
